key_insight: GS-BMT establishes a large donor–recipient genomic research platform for blood and marrow transplantation, rather than an AI drug-discovery program.
clinical_relevance: The initiative aims to improve individualized transplant risk prediction and donor selection, but clinical utility remains to be demonstrated.
method: Assemble 30,718 allogeneic transplant donor–recipient pairs from the United States, 2000–2019.
Generate genome-wide SNP genotyping, with sequencing and methylation profiling in selected subsets.
Compare clinical survival models in AML and assess inherited CHIP susceptibility using donor polygenic scores.
evidence_signal: Among 9,262 AML patients, clinical-only Cox, random survival forest, and deep neural network models showed similarly modest survival discrimination (C-indices 0.63, 0.62, and 0.62); CHIP polygenic scores were assessed in 19,750 donors.
watch_item: The reported CHIP risk thresholds rely on assumed effect sizes, not demonstrated clinical outcomes, and do not establish a basis for donor selection.
paper_title: Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT): An NCI-CIBMTR genomic medicine initiative in hematopoietic cell transplantation
